The plaintiff however filed an application praying for temporary mandatory injunction to direct the defendants to issue the approved Time-tables to the plaintiff for its vessels and to restrain the defendants from claiming other dues till disposal of the suit. The defendants contested the prayer for temporary mandatory injunction and the matter ultimately came up to this court at the instance of the plaintiff-appellant which was successful in obtaining an ad interim order of temporary injunction for issuance of the approved Time-tables to the plaintiff till disposal of the said suit. The aforesaid suit was ultimately heard in presence of both the parties by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka, who was pleased to dismiss the same by his judgment and decree dated 28.11.1989. Being aggrieved by the same, the plaintiff preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge, Dhaka and the same was numbered as Title Appeal No. 51 of 1990 and then transferred to the 1st Court of the learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka for disposal. The defendants/respondents entered appearance in the said appeal to contest the same. The plaintiff/ appellant thereafter filed an application on 19.5.92 praying for temporary mandatory injunction against the defendants/respondents directing them to issue the Time-tables to the plaintiff-appellant during the pendency of the appeal, so that the plying of the vessel of the plaintiff/appellant was not stopped and also prayed for direction upon the contesting defendant-respondent not to give effect to Memo No. FC/B-00/0/1504 dated 15.4.92. The copy of the said application was not of course served upon the defendants-respondents, but filed in the court.
